alt: Section 2, Natural resources, sits at the centre of four linked themes: the problems and opportunities of a developing country, effects on and conservation of the environment, sustainable development, and feasibility studies.
caption: Section 2 is where Paper 2’s four recurring themes are introduced.

alt: Water sits at the centre. Deforestation causes soil erosion, silting and flooding and speeds up the silting of dams and barrages, reducing their storage. Mineral extraction and inland fish farming both depend on water supply and quality.
caption: Linking the four resources turns separate lists into one argument about sustainability.

alt: A table with one row each for water, forests, minerals and fish, and columns for what the resource is used for, what damages it, what would make its use sustainable, and a named, located example to learn.
caption: Ask the same three questions of every resource, then add a named place.

alt: Two cards compare command words. “Identify” wants a named location or fact. “Evaluate” wants an environmental cost weighed against a development benefit, shown as a balance, and a judgement rather than a list.
caption: Identify names; evaluate weighs and judges.

alt: Paper 2 lasts 1 hour 30 minutes, is worth 75 marks and 50% of the qualification. Candidates answer three of five questions, each worth 25 marks in four parts, (a) to (d), built around maps, graphs, tables and photographs. Part (d) tests analysis and evaluation.
caption: Three questions, four parts each, ending with an evaluation in part (d).
